links.note: Why a multicellular body cannot reproduce by dividing cell by cell - the item is about the limits of fission as a reproductive mode (192); in multicellular organisms that same division is growth.
Placenta as the nourishing organ, its location in the uterus, and the ejection reflex at delivery - all uterus-side facts of the female system (202).
Uterus implants the zygote and the fallopian tube conducts the ovum and hosts fertilisation - both named in 202.
Radicle versus plumule - parts of the embryo formed after fertilisation, which 199 covers through zygote-to-seed development. No separate germination concept exists.
Pollen grain versus ovule - the male and female structures of the flower (198). The transfer between them would be 199.
Parents and offspring share a chromosome number because meiosis halves and fertilisation restores it - the mechanics of sexual reproduction (197).
Path of sperm from testis to exterior plus accessory-gland secretions - the male reproductive system end to end (201).
Diagram identified as binary fission in Amoeba from the cleaving nucleus and pseudopodia (192), not budding (193).
Defines fertilisation and distinguishes external from internal - the fusion of gametes that defines sexual reproduction (197). The site named in part (b) is a single fact from 202.
Unisexual versus bisexual, the distinction this chapter teaches through flowers such as papaya and mustard (198).
Implantation, placenta and the duration of pregnancy - the uterine side of the female system (202).
Names anther, style and ovary with their functions - floral structure (198); the pollen's journey along the style would be 199 but the item is a labelling task.
How oral pills prevent ovulation and why they can be harmful - hormonal contraception (204).

Viral and bacterial STDs plus reasons for contraception (204).
Germinated seed labelled radicle, plumule and cotyledon with functions - the seed that fertilisation produces (199).
Two viral and two bacterial STDs with prevention (204).
Pieces of a cut body each growing into a new individual, named as regeneration in Planaria and Hydra (194). Not 193 - the pieces are produced by cutting, not by the organism's own fragmentation.
Germination defined and a pollen-germination diagram corrected (male germ cell, pollen grain, pollen tube, ovule) - the pollination-to-fertilisation sequence (199).
Surgical contraception does not stop STDs, and how AIDS is prevented - both arms of 204.
How the uterus prepares and nurtures the embryo through the placenta (202). The closing clause about an unfertilised egg touches 203, but the item is built on the uterus preparing for pregnancy.
Functions of plumule, cotyledon and radicle in the seedling - post-fertilisation seed structure (199).
Chromosome number held constant in BOTH asexual (mitosis) and sexual (meiosis plus fertilisation) reproduction - the unifying idea is faithful DNA copying (190). 197 would only cover the sexual half.
Placenta and two major functions (202).
Pollen germinating on the stigma, pollen tube, and how the zygote is formed - fertilisation in plants (199).
Longitudinal section of a flower with anther, style, stigma and ovary labelled - floral structure (198).

Pollen germination on the stigma and the post-fertilisation changes in the flower (199).

Population explosion checked through fertility control and family planning - the contraception/reproductive-health concept (204).
